back: Profit from operations ÷ capital employed × 100. Capital employed = issued shares + all reserves + non-current liabilities.
Capital employed also equals total assets less current liabilities. Use it to check your figure.
Margin = mark-up ÷ (100 + mark-up) × 100. A 25% mark-up is a 20% margin.
Expenses ÷ revenue × 100. Shows how well operating costs are controlled.

front: Why is profit before interest used in ROCE?
back: Because capital employed includes the loan notes, whose reward is the interest; profit must be before finance costs and tax.
Profit for the year ÷ equity × 100. Return on assets divides by total assets. State the formula you use.

front: Explaining a fall in profit margin
back: Check gross margin first, then expenses to revenue, then finance costs and tax. Name the cause and quote the figures.
